items.prompt: Add -ness to kind. Which word do you make?

options.why: The suffix -ness ends in a double s.
That uses -ment, and kindment is not a word.
Kindly uses -ly, not -ness.

hints: The suffix -ness turns a describing word into a noun.
Kind does not change. Just add the suffix.
Check how many s letters the suffix has.
items.explanation: Kind + ness = kindness. The root word does not change, and -ness ends in a double s.

items.prompt: Add -ment to enjoy. Which word do you make?

options.why: That uses -ness, and enjoyness is not a word.
There is no e between enjoy and -ment.
Enjoyed is the past tense, not a -ment noun.

hints: The suffix -ment turns a verb into a noun.
Enjoy does not change. Just add the suffix.
Write enjoy, then add the four letters of the suffix.
items.explanation: Enjoy + ment = enjoyment. The y stays because a vowel comes before it.

items.prompt:
Add -ness to dark.
We could not see anything in the ___.
hints: You need a noun that names something.
Dark does not change before the suffix.
Check that your word ends in a double s.
items.explanation: Dark + ness = darkness. It names the state of being dark.

items.prompt:
Add -ment to move.
The dancer made a slow ___ with her arms.
hints: You need a noun after the words a slow.
Move ends in e. Keep the e before -ment.
Write move, then add the suffix.
items.explanation: Move + ment = movement. The e stays, because -ment starts with a consonant.

items.prompt: Sort the words. Which suffix makes a real noun?
hints: Say each word with -ness and then with -ment.
Only one suffix sounds like a real word each time.
Start with pay. Is it payness or payment?
items.explanation: We say sadness, kindness, darkness and illness. We say agreement, payment, amazement and excitement.

items.prompt:
Add -ness to happy.
On the last day of school, the children were full of ___.
hints: Happy ends in a consonant and then y.
Remember the rule for words like this. What happens to the y?
Think of happy and happily. Make the same change.
items.explanation: Happy ends in a consonant and y, so the y changes to i: happiness.

items.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?

options.why: Lazy ends in a consonant and y, so the y changes to i.
The suffix -ness has a double s.
There is no e after the i.

hints: Lazy ends in z and then y.
Change the y before adding the suffix.
Check that the end of the word is -ness with a double s.
items.explanation: Lazy ends in a consonant and y, so y changes to i. Lazy + ness = laziness.

items.prompt: Match each word to the noun made from it.
hints: Each word takes -ness or -ment.
Watch for words that change before the suffix.
Start with ill. Which noun means being ill?
items.explanation: Empty changes y to i to make emptiness. Argue drops its e to make argument. The others just add the suffix.

items.prompt: Ella gasped in ___ when she saw the huge cake.

options.why: Amaze takes -ment, not -ness.
Amazing describes something. After in, we need a noun.
Amazed describes how someone feels. After in, we need a noun.

hints: The missing word comes after in.
You need a noun that names a feeling.
Which suffix goes with amaze?
items.explanation: After in we need a noun. Amaze + ment = amazement.

items.prompt: Which pair is correct?

options.why: Argue drops its e before -ment. It is one of the tricky ones.
Silly ends in a consonant and y, so it becomes silliness.
Merry changes y to i: merriment.

hints: Check each root word for an e or a y at the end.
Words ending in a consonant and y change y to i.
Argue breaks the usual keep-the-e rule. Look closely at the two argue pairs.
items.explanation: Argue drops its e before -ment, so it is argument. Silly becomes silliness and merry becomes merriment.

items.prompt:
Add -ment to excite and to announce.
The team cheered with ___ after the ___.
hints: Both words end in e.
Most words ending in e keep the e before -ment.
Write excite, then add the suffix. Do the same for announce.
items.explanation: Excite + ment = excitement, and announce + ment = announcement. Both words keep their e.

items.prompt: Add -ness to sudden. Which spelling is right?

options.why: Sudden ends in n, and -ness starts with n, so you need both.
Do not drop the e from sudden.
The suffix -ness ends in a double s.

hints: Write sudden first.
Do not change sudden before adding the suffix.
Count the letter n where the two parts join.
items.explanation: Sudden + ness = suddenness. Sudden ends in n and -ness starts with n, so there are two n letters together.

items.prompt: Which word is a noun?

options.why: Sad describes someone. It is not the name of a feeling.
Sadly says how something is done.
Sadder compares two things.

hints: A noun names a thing or a feeling.
Which word could follow The?
Try: The ___ made her cry.
items.explanation: Sadness names a feeling, so it is a noun. -ness turns a describing word into a noun.

items.prompt: Add -ness to sad. Which word do you make?

options.why: Sad does not need an extra e.
The suffix is -ness, with two s letters.
Only one n comes from sad and one from -ness. Count them again.

hints: Write sad first.
Then add all of -ness.
Do not add or drop any letters.
items.explanation: Sad ends in d, so we just add -ness: sadness.

items.prompt: Add -ment to pay. Which word do you make?

options.why: Pay does not need an extra e.
Pay keeps its y when -ment is added.
The suffix is spelt -ment, with an e.

hints: Write the root word first.
Then add the whole suffix.
Check you keep the y.
items.explanation: Pay ends in y after a vowel, so it stays the same: payment.

items.prompt: Citra was full of ___ when she heard she had won.
hints: What kind of word follows full of?
You need the name of a feeling.
Which choice is a noun?
items.explanation: After full of we need a noun. Happiness is the noun made from happy.

items.prompt:
Add -ment to agree.
The two friends shook hands in ___.
hints: Write the root word first.
Add the suffix to the end.
Keep the last e of agree.
items.explanation: Agree ends in e, and the suffix -ment starts with m, so we keep the e: agreement.

items.prompt: Spell the noun for when there is no light.
items.sentence: We sat in the darkness and waited.
hints: Think of the root word first.
Add the suffix that makes a noun.
Dark plus ness has a double s.
items.explanation: Dark plus -ness gives darkness. The n and the s from -ness both stay.

items.prompt: Sort the root words by the suffix that makes a real noun.
hints: Try both suffixes with each word.
Say the noun aloud.
Start with equip. Is it equipness or equipment?
items.explanation: We say darkness, sadness and softness, and payment, movement and equipment.

items.prompt:
Add -ness to tidy.
Mum was pleased with the ___ of my room.
hints: The root word ends in y.
When y follows a consonant, it often changes before a suffix.
Change the y to i, then add -ness.
items.explanation: Tidy ends in y after a consonant, so y changes to i: tidiness.

items.prompt: Add -ness to open. Which spelling is right?

options.why: You need all of -ness. Open also ends in n.
The suffix -ness ends in two s letters.
Do not drop letters from open.

hints: Write open, then add -ness.
Both n letters stay: one from open, one from -ness.
Count the s letters at the end.
items.explanation: Open ends in n and -ness starts with n, so both stay: openness.

items.prompt: Build a sentence about a feeling. Use a noun made with -ment.
items.answer: Her excitement grew as the bus arrived.
hints: The sentence starts with a capital letter.
Choose the noun that ends in -ment.
Her goes first. Then the noun.
items.explanation: Excitement is the noun made from excite with -ment.

items.prompt: Which pair is spelt correctly?

options.why: Pay keeps its y before -ment.
Happy changes y to i before -ness.
Pay does not need an extra e.

hints: Check each word on its own.
Look at what happens to y before a suffix.
Pay keeps y after a vowel. Happy changes y after a consonant.
items.explanation: Payment keeps its y after a vowel. Happy ends in y after a consonant, so it becomes happiness.

items.prompt: Match each word to the noun made from it.
hints: All of these roots end in y.
Change y to i, then add -ness.
Start with dizzy. Watch the double z.
items.explanation: Each word ends in y after a consonant, so y changes to i before -ness.

items.prompt: Choose all the nouns made by adding -ness or -ment.

options.why: Careful is made with -ful and describes someone.
Quickly is made with -ly and says how.
Useless is made with -less and describes something.

hints: Look at the end of each word.
Only -ness and -ment are wanted.
Then check the word names something.
items.explanation: Kindness, enjoyment and argument are nouns made with -ness or -ment. The others use -ful, -ly and -less.

items.prompt: Which word is NOT made by adding -ment to a root word?

options.why: This is agree plus -ment.
This is move plus -ment.
This is treat plus -ment.

hints: Cover the ending -ment.
Is what is left a real word with a matching meaning?
Check ce.
items.explanation: Ce is not a word, so cement is just one word. The others are root words plus -ment.

items.prompt:
Add -ness to weak and -ment to replace.
The ___ of the old engine meant it needed a ___.
hints: Fill the gaps in order.
Replace ends in e, so think about that e.
Keep the e: replace plus -ment.
items.explanation: Weak plus -ness is weakness. Replace plus -ment is replacement, and the e stays.

items.prompt: What does the suffix -ness usually do to a word?

options.text: It turns a describing word into a noun.
It turns the word into a verb.
options.why: Verbs are doing words. -ness names a quality.

options.text: It makes the word mean not.
options.why: Not is the job of prefixes like un-.

options.text: It makes the word mean again.
options.why: Again is the job of the prefix re-.

hints: Think of kind and kindness.
Is kindness a describing word or a name?
Look at how the word is used in a sentence.
items.explanation: -ness turns a describing word like kind into a noun like kindness.

items.prompt: Forgetfulness is made with two suffixes. Which are they, in order?

options.why: -ness comes last because it makes the final noun.
There is no -ment in this word.
There is no -ly in this word.

hints: Start with the root word forget.
Build the word one step at a time.
forget, then forgetful, then forgetfulness.
items.explanation: Forget plus -ful makes forgetful. Then -ness makes the noun forgetfulness.

items.prompt: Spell the noun for the sad feeling when something does not go as you hoped.
items.sentence: Her disappointment was clear when the trip was cancelled.
hints: It begins with a prefix.
Count the letters: one s, two p, one n, one t before -ment.
Say the root in parts: dis, ap, point.
items.explanation: Disappointment is dis- plus appoint plus -ment. It has one s and two p letters.

items.prompt: True or false: Adding -ness to the word kind makes the noun kindness.
hints: Look at the end of the new word.
Kindness names a quality.
Add n, e, s, s to kind.
items.explanation: The suffix -ness turns an adjective into a noun. Kind becomes kindness.

items.prompt: True or false: Adding -ness to the word sad gives the spelling sadnes.
hints: The suffix has two s letters.
Check how -ness is spelt.
Sad plus ness is sadness.
items.explanation: The word sad ends in d, and -ness keeps both s letters, so the spelling is sadness.

items.prompt: True or false: When -ness is added to happy, the y changes to i to make happiness.
hints: Look at the letter before the y.
Happy ends in p then y.
The y changes to i.
items.explanation: When a word ends in a consonant plus y, change the y to i before adding -ness. Happy becomes happiness.

items.prompt: True or false: The word agreement is made by adding -ment to the word agree.
hints: Take away the ending and see what is left.
Agree is a verb.
Add -ment to the verb.
items.explanation: The suffix -ment makes a noun from a verb. Agree plus -ment is agreement, as in enjoy and enjoyment.

items.prompt: Add -ness to kind: ___.
hints: The suffix makes a noun.
kind + ness
Two s letters.
items.explanation: Kind plus -ness makes kindness.
